mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen in 3 of the last 4 weeks (-48.9 to -41.9), indicating positive momentum in discretionary outings. This autocorrelated recovery trend is expected to persist, pushing the next 4-week mean above the last 4-week mean.
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC improved from -48.9 to -41.9 over the last 3 weeks
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC reverses to below -45 for two consecutive weeks following the decision point, breaking the observed momentum.

mechanism_narrative: A week-on-week TRANSIT rebound exceeding 5 points signals renewed willingness to travel for non-essential purposes, which mechanically feeds into retail and recreation visits within two weeks as commuters resume stopping at stores.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises more than 5 points week-on-week (as it did from -47.9 to -41.4)
evidence_refs: fact:TRANSIT rose from -47.9 at t-2w to -39.7 at t-0w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to rise within 2 weeks after a TRANSIT rebound of this magnitude, or falls despite the TRANSIT increase persisting.

mechanism_narrative: WORKPLACES mobility has remained flat near -45 for four weeks despite TRANSIT recovering, suggesting that office-return policies (not transit capacity) are the binding constraint on weekday retail traffic. The interaction of stagnant WORKPLACES with rising TRANSIT implies retail gains will be capped and concentrated in weekend/leisure categories, limiting overall RETAIL_REC growth.
candidate_trigger: WORKPLACES stays within +/-2 points of -45 while TRANSIT rises more than 5 points
evidence_refs: fact:WORKPLACES ranged only -45.0 to -50.4 across all four weeks while TRANSIT rose
regime_hint: partial reopening with remote-work policy intact
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC rises by more than 5 points over the next 4 weeks despite WORKPLACES remaining flat, indicating the office-policy constraint is not binding.

mechanism_narrative: The sharp PARKS and RETAIL_REC dip at t-2w coinciding with a RESIDENTIAL peak (11.4) matches a holiday-period disruption (e.g., Christmas/New Year), after which normal activity patterns resume. In a post-holiday normalization regime, RETAIL_REC should continue rebounding toward pre-holiday levels over the next 2 weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL peaks and PARKS/RETAIL_REC trough in the same week, followed by RESIDENTIAL decline
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS fell to -24.3 and RESIDENTIAL peaked at 11.4 at t-2w, then both reverted
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC fails to exceed its t-0w level within 2 weeks, indicating the dip was not holiday-driven but reflects a durable new restriction.

mechanism_narrative: GROCERY_PHARM's strong recovery (-22.9 to -14.4) functions as a leading indicator of household willingness to leave home for non-essential errands. Once GROCERY_PHARM crosses above -15, consumers typically extend trips to include discretionary retail within one week.
evidence_refs: fact:GROCERY_PHARM reached -14.4 at t-0w, its highest value in the snapshot
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC does not rise in the week immediately following GROCERY_PHARM crossing -15, or declines despite the crossing.

mechanism_narrative: Elevated RESIDENTIAL time (sustained near 10-11 across all weeks) combined with recovering TRANSIT suggests people are making short, purposeful outbound trips rather than resuming full daily routines. This interaction pattern predicts a muted, short-horizon bump in RETAIL_REC rather than a sustained rise.
evidence_refs: fact:RESIDENTIAL stayed between 10.0 and 11.4 all four weeks while TRANSIT improved
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC shows a sustained multi-week rise rather than a single-week bump, or RESIDENTIAL spikes upward instead of staying flat.

mechanism_narrative: If local authorities reintroduce capacity restrictions on retail and recreation venues (regime: tightening restrictions), the currently observed recovery in RETAIL_REC, TRANSIT, and GROCERY_PHARM will reverse sharply, as occurred at t-2w when all series dropped simultaneously.
candidate_trigger: a simultaneous multi-series drop exceeding 5 points in the same week, mirroring the t-2w pattern
evidence_refs: fact:RETAIL_REC, TRANSIT, and GROCERY_PHARM all dropped together at t-2w
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC continues rising over the next 4 weeks even if a new restriction announcement occurs, indicating policy is not the binding driver.

mechanism_narrative: PARKS mobility shows high week-to-week volatility (-7.7, -24.3, -14.9, -7.0) consistent with winter weather sensitivity rather than policy change. This volatility is weather-driven noise uncorrelated with the underlying RETAIL_REC trend, so RETAIL_REC's near-term direction should be judged independent of PARKS swings.
evidence_refs: fact:PARKS swung between -24.3 and -7.0 within four weeks while RETAIL_REC trended steadily upward
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC direction tracks PARKS swings closely (correlation above 0.7), indicating PARKS volatility is not independent noise but a shared driver.
